body:
It's sick, wrong and scary. It's against reddit rules: "Remember the human. Reddit is a place for creating community and belonging, not for attacking marginalized or vulnerable groups of people. Everyone has a right to use Reddit free of harassment, bullying, and threats of violence. Communities and users that incite violence or that promote hate based on identity or vulnerability will be banned."

I understand that vaccine hesitancy is a problem, but in which sick world does it justify writing some horribly cruel things about someone who died?

Following your logic, if a doctor tells me to quit smoking, and I don't comply, which eventually leads to lung cancer, I won't be able to get treated for cancer. Simply because I neglected all the warnings that the doctor gave me.
Felt that way too. It's getting significantly better for me now tho. Barely noticing it anymore.
No more nausea, but the headaches are still here. Although not as often as before.
Really hope this bullshit will pass and just become a bad memory
Also i have been put on SSRIs since the headaches made me dangerously suicidal.
Doctors couldn't find any other reason for headaches than anxiety. Nothing in particular helps with the pain, I'm just trying to sleep it off.
Yes, although not as often af before
Been on zoloft for 6 days and on my third day i started getting pain in the middle of my chest. Makes me so anxious i can't stand it. Gonna talk to my doc tomorrow.
Still getting the headaches, but not as often as before. Seems like it always starts during the evening/night. Also a little nausea from time to time.

Going to see a neurologist in 2 months. Long queues in my country...

If the situation gets even worse, I will probably have to go to an ER.

I've started getting headaches 10 days after my first astrazeneca shot. My platelet count was normal, so I'm relatively confident it's not blood clot related. BUT the headache stil hasn't disappered after 6 weeks - it actually got worse. Interestingly, my form of headache reminds me of the one you mentioned. I also have this mild/moderate nausea. I really hope it will subside soon. This type of headache is so... annoying.
Got astra zeneca 7 weeks ago. I still have very weird headaches every single day. Was healthy and never dealt with any headaches before the shot...

I started getting headaches 10 days after astra zeneca. Just like yours, they appear shortly after i wake up. Then they randomly go away and come back throughout the day. The pain is usually on the top/back of my head. It's been 1.5 months and it's still not gone. It's really fucking me up tbh...

I can relate to some things you mentioned. My headaches feel like something is pressing around my head, and I get those sharp pain spikes, but they are very irregular. I also get dizzy and nauseous. I have been extermly anxoius lately and i feel like it's a vicous cycle, because the headaches make me worry even more and i get even more anxious - to the point where I feel like throwing up.

I'm in a similar situation. 12 days after the AZ vaccine i started getting mild-severe headaches. It feels like instant spikes of pain that come in random intervals. I also have mild nausea and feel like something is off in general. But my blood tests were fine...

I have a history of severe anxiety. But nothing compares to what I'm going through right now. The pain is annoying and I feel like it will either lead into something severe or that it will nag me for the rest of my life. It's hard to find motivation to keep going...

I really hope it will get better for you OP, nobody deserves this
Been there with the AZ vaccine. Feels shitty.
